findings.rationale: WI's uploaded updates are anti-aligned with the coordinate-wise median update: mean cosine -0.75 across 20 rounds (noise-adjusted z -10.5), min cos -0.98. Per-round check shows negative cosine from round 1 (cos -1.0 in round 1, -1.0 in round 2, and negative in nearly every round through round 19). Norm ratios are normal (about 0.7-1.5), so this is a direction-reversal (sign-flip style) manipulation rather than scaling. Local performance looks normal (AUC 0.793, CITL ~0), which argues against label noise, so the anomaly sits in the uploaded update rather than the data.

SC's updates are strongly anti-aligned with the median: mean cosine -0.52 (noise-adjusted z -8.7), min cos -0.99. Per-round cosine is negative from round 1 (-0.70) and stays negative in almost all rounds (only round 13 is positive). Norm ratios are normal. Local AUC (0.805) and CITL (-0.03) are within the normal range, so the local data look fine and the anomaly is in the uploaded update, consistent with poisoning.

HI's updates are anti-aligned with the median: mean cosine -0.51 (noise-adjusted z -8.6), min cos -0.97. Per-round cosine is -1.0 in round 1 and strongly negative through round 8, then weaker but still negative in most later rounds. Norm ratios are normal. Local AUC (0.805) and CITL (-0.007) look normal, so the local data do not explain the anomaly and it points to a manipulated upload from the start.

report.summary: I screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Three clients (HI, SC, WI) show a consistent, strongly anti-aligned update direction from round 1 (noise-adjusted z between -8.6 and -10.5), with normal norms and normal local AUC/CITL. That pattern fits poisoning, not label noise, so I report them as poisoning with onset round 1. Other leads did not hold up on confirmation: NC, ND, MS and GU feature-tail outliers were not reproduced at round 20 with narrower queries; GU's O/E excess is similar across both sexes and its CITL is only about 1.8 SE from zero, so it is not a subgroup-specific bias or a clear prevalence shift; WI's AgeGroup and Sex deviations, DC's small-sample outliers, and the drift-tool CITL values (e.g. NV, VI, GU) were too noisy or inconsistent with the performance table to act on. Budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
